title: Agarose Gel Electrophoresis
author: Alba Balletbó
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.7ukhnuw

steps.title: Prepare agarose solution
steps.instruction: Measure 1 g of agarose (Thermo Fisher catalog #75510019). Typical gels are 0.7 %–2 % agarose; for example, 2 g in 100 mL 0.5× TAE yields a 2 % gel.

steps.title: Dissolve agarose in buffer
steps.instruction: Add the agarose powder to 100 mL 0.5× TAE in a microwavable flask (TBE may be used instead, but the same buffer must be used later in the gel box).

steps.title: Microwave agarose mixture
steps.instruction: Microwave the flask for 1–3 min until the agarose is completely dissolved, avoiding over‑boiling. It is advisable to microwave in 30–45 s pulses, stopping to swirl the flask each time; watch for boil‑over and use a watch‑glass or saran wrap if needed.

steps.title: Cool agarose to 50 °C
steps.instruction: Allow the molten agarose to cool to about 50 °C (approximately 5 min, the point at which you can comfortably hold the flask with your hand).

steps.title: Add SYBR Safe stain
steps.instruction: Add SYBR™ Safe DNA Gel Stain to a final concentration of 0.1 µL / mL (10 µL per 100 mL gel). Use the Invitrogen‑Thermo Fisher product (catalog #S33102).

steps.title: Pour gel into casting tray
steps.instruction: Place the well comb in the gel tray and slowly pour the agarose solution to avoid bubbles. Any bubbles can be pushed away from the comb with a pipette tip.

steps.title: Solidify gel
steps.instruction: Let the gel set until completely solidified: either place the tray at 4 °C for 10–15 min or let it sit at room temperature for 20–30 min.

steps.title: Prepare DNA samples with loading dye
steps.instruction: Add Gel Loading Dye, Purple (6×, no SDS) to each DNA sample (4.0 mL, New England Biolabs catalog #B7025S). The dye provides visual tracking and glycerol increases sample density.

steps.title: Insert gel into electrophoresis unit
steps.instruction: Place the solidified gel into the electrophoresis box (gel box).

steps.title: Fill gel box with running buffer
steps.instruction: Fill the gel box with 0.5× TAE (or TBE) until the gel is fully covered.

steps.title: Load molecular weight ladder
steps.instruction: Load a molecular‑weight ladder into the first lane: 100 bp DNA Ladder (New England Biolabs catalog #N3231L, 500 lanes) or 1 kb DNA Ladder (catalog #N3232L, 1,000 lanes). Place the pipette tip just above the well, apply gentle pressure, and withdraw the tip after the sample has entered the well.

steps.title: Load DNA samples
steps.instruction: Load each prepared DNA sample into the remaining wells using the same careful technique to avoid bubbles or buffer entry.

steps.title: Run electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Run the gel at 80–150 V until the tracking dye front has migrated 75–80 % of the gel length (typically 1–1.5 h, depending on gel concentration and voltage).

steps.title: Stop run and remove gel
steps.instruction: Turn off the power, disconnect the electrodes, and carefully lift the gel out of the box.

steps.title: Visualize DNA under UV
steps.instruction: Place the gel on a UV transilluminator and view the DNA bands. Wear safety goggles, face shield, gloves, and a lab coat. If downstream purification is required, use long‑wavelength UV and minimize exposure time.

steps.title: Determine fragment sizes
steps.instruction: Compare the positions of sample bands to the ladder in the first lane (manufacturer’s size chart) to estimate fragment sizes.

steps.title: Excise desired DNA band
steps.instruction: Using a sterilized razor blade, cut out the band of interest, taking as little surrounding gel as possible (excess gel may exceed the capacity of purification kits).

steps.title: Collect gel slice in tube
steps.instruction: Transfer the gel slice to a microcentrifuge tube and weigh it for downstream calculations.

steps.title: Purify DNA with cleanup kit
steps.instruction: Isolate the DNA from the gel slice using a commercial gel‑purification kit (Macherey‑Nagel Gel and PCR Clean‑up Kit, catalog #740609.250) according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
